messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a full intake sweep on the nightly branch and hit bench-saturation spikes. slowest probe hit ~12s and that cascaded into validator timeouts -> fallback path. repro: `./scripts/run-smoke --batch 2000 --seed 42`. logs:
```
prober: request=0xabc status=503 latency_ms=12034
validator: error=timeout stage=heavy_eval
```
Anyone else seeing this?
aj: yikes. which runner/config? dedicated prober or shared runner?
maria: shared runner. config used: `ingest.concurrency=8`, `bench.window=30s`. seems batching balloons when seqlen distribution skews.
kevin: cc @lina @dmitri — this smells like the deferred-bench design we discussed in the RFC (non-blocking heavy_eval). If heavy_eval waits on KV warmups we get tail latencies. question: do we decouple validator (async ack + reconcile) or keep strict sync semantics?
lina: leaning async ack + canary fast-path. flow: accept -> prober-lite -> async heavy_eval. need compensating signals for quality drift (alerts + per-tenant late-finish metrics). otherwise product will see higher latency or more denials.
dmitri: agree on async, but cost/complexity tradeoffs: bookkeeping, tombstones, and ordering. we could add an immediate "golden-check" quick-run (1-2 samples) synchronously to catch gross regressions, then let heavy_eval run async.
aj: quick practical idea: add `admit.early_check=true` to pipeline to run tiny golden sample before commit. ~10-30ms extra but avoids egregious regressions slipping through.
maria: if we adopt that, upstream interface needs to change because callers expect an immediate final `admit_result`. propose returning `{status: provisional|final, admit_id}` and a webhook/callback when final is complete. backcompat via `admit.sync=true` default for existing clients.
kevin: that matches my thinking. migration plan sketch: 1) feature-flag the async path, 2) opt-in for high-throughput tenants, 3) graceful degrade for sync-only clients. telemetry to add: `admitted.provisional_count`, `late_finalize_count`, `failback_rate`, and `provisional_latency_p95`.
lina: also add a saturation guard: if heavy_eval backlog > N then force reject with `reason=prober_saturated` instead of enqueueing forever. easier to reason about and surfaces the problem.
maria: I'll draft an RFC update with diagrams and concrete payload examples. aiming for a PR by EOW. assigning draft to me. :thumbsup:
aj: +1, ping me and I can review the perf/memory implications.
sre-bot: Deploy window note: no deploys during 23:00-05:00 UTC. (auto message)
maria: thanks — will post the draft in #eng-ml-rfcs when ready.
